# omadafusion_group (Resource)

An IP group or IP-port group (Profiles > Groups) for use in ACLs. The controller does not support editing groups in place, so every change replaces the group. Note: on Fusion 6.3.x, groups that list the gateway's own addresses do not match traffic addressed to the gateway; use `destination_type = 5` on the ACL instead.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "omadafusion_group" "printers" {
  name    = "Printers"
  type    = "ip"
  subnets = [{ cidr = "192.168.30.10/32", description = "front desk" }]
}

resource "omadafusion_group" "admin_ports" {
  name    = "Admin ports"
  type    = "ip_port"
  subnets = [{ cidr = "192.168.10.0/24" }]
  ports   = ["22", "443", "8043"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Group name.
- `subnets` (Attributes List) Members in CIDR form, e.g. `192.168.10.0/24` or `192.168.10.5/32`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subnets))

### Optional

- `ports` (List of String) Ports or ranges (`"22"`, `"8000-8100"`). Required for `ip_port`, not allowed for `ip`.
- `site` (String) Site name or ID. Defaults to the provider `site`. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `type` (String) `ip` (IP group) or `ip_port` (IP-port group). Defaults to `ip`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Group ID.

<a id="nestedatt--subnets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `subnets`

Required:

- `cidr` (String) IPv4 address with prefix length.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Member description.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <id> or <site>/<id>
terraform import omadafusion_group.printers Default/64f0c0ffee00000000000001
```
